_comment: Reviewed license inventory for every Python distribution that may be installed in
a validation or consumer environment. tools/check_licenses.py compares installed
metadata against it. Add a reviewed entry before adding a dependency; a missing
entry fails the check. Human-readable table: docs/third-party.md.
'bundled' describes what a distribution's wheels ship inside themselves (native
libraries, statically linked code, fonts); 'bundled_files' records each separate
shared library by glob (POSIX path relative to site-packages, as in RECORD),
SPDX expression, linkage and the CI platforms where it was found. Surveyed for
the pinned CPython 3.12 wheels on manylinux x86_64, macOS arm64 and Windows amd64;
tool wheels that only the Linux job installs (cryptography, cffi, nh3) on

rules: Licenses are judged at three levels: what this repository creates, copies, builds, links or distributes; each distribution by the license it declares; components bundled inside third-party wheels, which are recorded and reviewed, not banned
runtime and optional (non-test extras of first-party packages): permissive only; the policy would allow weak copyleft in optional extras, but this repository stays stricter
test (extras named in test_extras) and tool: permissive, or weak copyleft when the entry sets test_only
GPL: only entries with external_process (a separate process, as a reference tool or an optional backend); never a base runtime requirement, and first-party code must not import them

never_families (AGPL and other network copyleft): any identifier of the family (every version, deprecated ids, '+' forms and LicenseRef- names) in an entry, a bundled_files record or installed metadata is rejected in every environment, also as an external process

bundled_files: every shared library a third-party distribution installs, other than its own Python extension modules, must match a glob recorded for the current OS; a record needs a review unless its expression is satisfied by permissive plus bundled_permissive (reviewed permissive ids accepted only for bundled files) and names no copyleft license; first-party distributions contain no native files
bundled_files of entries without external_process load into the OpenPhysics process: a GPL term passes only with a listed runtime exception (runtime_exceptions) or inside an OR with another option

light.reason: Material cavity order-4 cases take 25-63 s and peak at 1.8 GB; no stored record has been added yet.

array-api-compat.review: Runtime requirement of galerkin (galerkin.core.backend); pure Python.

certifi.review: CA bundle used unmodified (certifi's bundle is itself derived from Mozilla's), pulled in by httpx (simcase test extra) and requests (twine). Not a runtime dependency and never redistributed.

cffi.bundled: Linux job only: _cffi_backend statically contains libffi (MIT; its ffi_* symbols are exported, no separate library). The wheel carries only cffi's own MIT-0 license, no libffi notice.

cryptography.bundled: Linux job only: the _rust extension module statically links OpenSSL 4.0.3 (Apache-2.0; the wheel's SBOM records a no-shared build) and Rust crates, mostly MIT OR Apache-2.0, also BSD-3-Clause, Unicode-3.0 (unicode-ident) and self_cell (Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only, used under Apache-2.0). The wheel's CycloneDX SBOMs list them; its license files cover cryptography itself.

docutils.metadata_review: The GPL classifier refers to files outside the wheel; COPYING.rst lists the shipped modules as public domain, BSD-2-Clause or 0BSD (eLyXer-derived files were relicensed to BSD-2-Clause). Reached only through twine's README check.

gmsh.review: GPL-2.0-or-later with an exception permitting combination with Netgen, METIS, OpenCASCADE and ParaView (LICENSE.txt in the wheel). Optional backend of gmshio[gmsh] and a CI tool. Only the gmsh command is run, as a separate process (from the pip wheel it is a launcher script that loads Gmsh's own Python module and libgmsh in that process); its .msh output is read by original parsers. Never imported by first-party code or bundled.

bundled_files.review: Gmsh's own library (GPL-2.0-or-later with the Gmsh exception), installed by the gmsh wheel as a data file outside site-packages and loaded only by Gmsh's Python module inside the separate gmsh process. First-party code never imports gmsh (forbidden_imports).

Gmsh's own library (GPL-2.0-or-later with the Gmsh exception), installed by the gmsh wheel as a data file outside site-packages and loaded only by Gmsh's Python module inside the separate gmsh process. First-party code never imports gmsh (forbidden_imports).

jaxlib.bundled: jaxlib's own compiled modules (jaxlib/*.so and its cpu/ and mlir/_mlir_libs/ subfolders, Python extension modules without a version tag, and libjax_common.so) statically contain the components whose licenses the wheel's LICENSE.txt reproduces: BoringSSL, gRPC, Abseil, Protocol Buffers, RE2, DLPack, double-conversion, Eigen (MPL-2.0, file-level weak copyleft, compiled by the wheel's publisher and used as shipped), Farmhash, FlatBuffers, HighwayHash, libjpeg-turbo, fft2d, giflib, LLVM (Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception), oneDNN, nsync, TensorFlow, pybind11, snappy, upb and zlib. No separately built third-party library. Checked on Linux, jaxlib 0.12.0.1 (RECORD and LICENSE.txt). Reviewed with Wavebit's entry for the same release (fieldalgo/wavebit main 051bcae, tools/third_party_licenses.json).

bundled_files.review: jaxlib's own compiled modules (fnmatch '*' also matches the cpu/ and mlir/_mlir_libs/ subfolders), loaded by jax; their static contents are listed under 'bundled'. galerkin only calls jax's Python API and does not modify, relink or redistribute them.

matplotlib.review: PSF-based permissive license agreement; no SPDX identifier exists for it.
matplotlib.bundled: Extension modules statically include FreeType (FTL OR GPL-2.0-or-later, FTL relied on), HarfBuzz (MIT-Modern-Variant), libraqm (MIT), SheenBidi (Apache-2.0) and Qhull (Qhull license); data files include fonts under OFL-1.1 (STIX, Last Resort), the BaKoMa Fonts Licence, Bitstream Vera terms (DejaVu) and Adobe AFM terms. No separate shared libraries.

meshio.review: simcase[export] optional extra for VTU export; pure Python, requires numpy and rich.

nh3.bundled: Linux job only (twine dependency): the extension module statically links Rust crates, mostly MIT OR Apache-2.0 or MIT, ICU4X crates under Unicode-3.0, and cssparser and dtoa-short under MPL-2.0 (file-level weak copyleft, compiled by the wheel's publisher and used as shipped). The wheel carries nh3's MIT license and a CycloneDX SBOM listing the crates. A CI tool, never imported by package code and not redistributed.

numpy.spdx: BSD-3-Clause AND 0BSD AND MIT AND Zlib AND CC0-1.0
numpy.bundled: Linux and macOS before 14: OpenBLAS with LAPACK (BSD-3-Clause, BSD-3-Clause-Open-MPI), libgfortran (and libgcc_s on macOS; GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1) and libquadmath (LGPL-2.1-or-later, not covered by the GCC exception) as separate shared libraries. macOS 14 and later: nothing bundled (Apple Accelerate). Windows: OpenBLAS DLL with the GCC runtime and winpthreads (MIT AND BSD-3-Clause) statically linked, plus msvcp140.dll (Microsoft redistributable terms, no notice in the wheel).

bundled_files.review: GCC runtime under the GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1; loaded by the wheel's own OpenBLAS or extension modules, not by OpenPhysics package code. Not redistributed.

pillow.bundled: Linux and macOS: 18 image, font and compression libraries as separate shared libraries, all permissive per the wheel's notice; FreeType is FTL OR GPL-2.0-or-later (FTL relied on); the xz section's LGPL/GPL text covers command-line tools that are not included, and its 'liblzma is in the public domain' line is pre-5.6 xz wording: the bundled xz 5.8.3 liblzma is 0BSD upstream. Windows: the same codecs statically linked into the extension modules. FriBiDi (LGPL) is not bundled; Pillow loads it at run time only if the system provides it.

bundled_files.review: FreeType is dual-licensed; the FreeType License (FTL) option is relied on, which requires a credit when binaries are redistributed. Loaded by Pillow's extension modules. Not redistributed.

pip.bundled: Vendors certifi's CA bundle (MPL-2.0), used unmodified, and other permissive pure-Python packages. Also ships distlib's Windows launcher executables (pip/_vendor/distlib/t*.exe, w*.exe; 32-bit, 64-bit, ARM64), built from distlib's PC/launcher.c (BSD-2-Clause); they import no C runtime DLL. Installed on every OS, run only on Windows. The wheel carries distlib's PSF-2.0 license text, not the launcher's BSD notice.

pydantic-core.bundled: Statically links Rust crates under MIT, Apache-2.0, Unlicense OR MIT and Unicode-3.0 (icu_normalizer); the wheel carries only pydantic-core's own MIT license.

pyyaml.bundled: Statically includes libyaml (MIT) in the _yaml extension module.

scikit-fem.review: Reference tool for code-to-code comparisons, galerkin[crosscheck] test extra; pure Python, requires only numpy and scipy.

scipy.bundled: Linux: OpenBLAS with LAPACK (BSD-3-Clause, BSD-3-Clause-Open-MPI) and two builds each of libgfortran (GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1) and libquadmath (LGPL-2.1-or-later) as separate shared libraries. macOS (all versions): libgfortran, libgcc_s and libquadmath, plus OpenBLAS before macOS 14. Windows: OpenBLAS DLL with the GCC runtime and winpthreads statically linked; scipy/odr/__odrpack also statically contains GCC runtime code, very likely including libquadmath (byte-level match), and winpthreads appears in several extension modules; the wheel's notice mentions only the DLL. Qhull (Qhull license) is statically linked on every platform.

setuptools.bundled: Windows launcher executables (setuptools/cli*.exe, gui*.exe; 32-bit, 64-bit, ARM64) built from setuptools' own launcher.c (MIT); they load the Microsoft C runtime (VCRUNTIME140.dll, Universal CRT) from the system. Installed on every OS, run only on Windows.

shapely.bundled: Linux, macOS and Windows: GEOS (LGPL-2.1, no 'or later' stated) as separate shared libraries geos and geos_c, built from the upstream release without patches and renamed by wheel repair tools; LICENSE_GEOS carries the full LGPL-2.1 text but no GEOS copyright line. Windows also bundles msvcp140.dll (Microsoft redistributable terms, LICENSE_win32). OpenPhysics does not redistribute shapely or GEOS.

symfem.review: Reference for element definitions, galerkin[crosscheck] test extra; pure Python, requires sympy and appdirs. Its wheel metadata declares no license field; the MIT text ships as the wheel's license file.

sympy.review: Required by symfem (galerkin[crosscheck] test extra); pure Python. Metadata says only BSD; its LICENSE adds code from Diofant, multipledispatch and PyDy (BSD-3-Clause) and sympy/parsing/latex from latex2sympy (MIT).

torch.spdx: Apache-2.0 AND Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception AND BSD-2-Clause AND BSD-3-Clause AND BSL-1.0 AND MIT
torch.bundled: Linux CPU wheel (the one CI installs, from download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu): torch's own libraries in torch/lib/ (libtorch, libtorch_cpu, libtorch_python, libtorch_global_deps, libc10, libshm and the test or example libraries libaoti_custom_ops, libbackend_with_compiler, libjitbackend_test and libtorchbind_test) statically contain the third-party code whose licenses the wheel's dist-info/licenses/third_party/ reproduces (35 projects, among them XNNPACK, NNPACK, fbgemm, sleef, protobuf, onnx, pybind11 and llvm-openmp), plus GNU libgomp (GCC's OpenMP runtime; symbol versions GOMP_* and GOACC_*) as a separate shared library. Read on Linux from torch 2.14.1+cpu (RECORD, licenses, libgomp symbol versions); agrees with Wavebit's entry for the same wheel (fieldalgo/wavebit main 051bcae). The Linux PyPI wheel instead requires NVIDIA CUDA packages (cuda-toolkit, nvidia-*-cu13); per HQ decision 2026-10-26-torch-cuda-dependencies-acceptable they are torch's own dependencies and are not reviewed or matched here.

bundled_files.review: GNU libgomp under the GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1; loaded by torch's own libraries, not by galerkin code. Not redistributed.
